www.bizdaily.co.kr/news/1118-02:
Regulator begins year-end inspections of payment processors
[Article]
Section: Economy
By: Han Soyun
Published: 2024.11.18 06:30
Financial authorities will begin their regular year-end inspection of electronic payment processors on Monday. The check is an industry-wide review held every second half, and this year it will look first at registered firms whose transaction volume exceeds a set threshold.
Written reviews will run through the end of the month, followed by on-site visits to individual companies starting in December. The main items are settlement cycles, handling of merchant funds, response procedures for system outages and personal data protection.
The industry is busy preparing. Many firms are organizing their documents ahead of time, and mid-sized players such as CorpX, which recently passed 10,000 merchants, are reported to have moved up their internal reviews. An official at a large payment processor said, "This is a routine annual inspection, so nothing unusual. The hardest part is meeting the submission deadline."
Park Seongwoo, secretary general of the Korea Electronic Payment Association, said, "Some forms for the written review changed this year, so we notified members of the changes and held a briefing."
The authorities plan to compile the results in the first quarter of next year and share them with the industry. Deficiencies will be flagged for correction, while minor items will be explained on the spot.

Base rate held; year-end lending market catches its breath
[Article]
Section: Economy
By: Oh Taegyeong
Published: 2024.11.19 07:10
The central bank's monetary policy committee held the base rate at 3.25% on Tuesday. The decision matched market expectations, and the committee said it needed to watch inflation and the growth in household debt a while longer.
Loan counters at commercial banks were relatively calm after the news. Floating mortgage rates were little changed from a week earlier, and some banks are continuing year-end preferential rate promotions.
"Loan demand usually slows toward the end of the year, so the impact of this hold on the market is limited," said Yoon Sera, senior research fellow at the Future Economy Institute. "The direction of rates in the first half of next year depends on inflation and the exchange rate."
The burden on self-employed owners and small businesses remains. Companies with loans coming due expect rates to stay high for some time and are redrawing their repayment plans.
The committee will meet next in January. Most observers expect the lending market to stay on the sidelines until then.

CorpX Pay passes 10,000 merchants, expands settlement reports
[Article]
Section: IT
By: Seo Minji
Published: 2024.10.21 09:00
Payment service CorpX Pay, run by enterprise software maker CorpX, passed 10,000 merchants on Monday, ten years after its launch in 2014.
CorpX said it will expand its settlement report features to keep pace with merchant growth. Daily and weekly settlement details can now be compared on one screen, and fees and refunds can be downloaded by item.
According to the company, monthly payment volume is about KRW 120 billion across a mix of online shops, local retailers and hospitals. The company is headquartered at CorpX Tower on Teheran-ro in Seoul and has 412 employees.
"As the number of merchants grows, so does the demand for accurate and transparent settlement," said CEO Kang Taeho. "We will improve the reports so merchant owners can follow their sales easily."
Industry watchers see it as an example of a mid-sized player differentiating itself through settlement convenience while the payment market consolidates around its largest firms.

SME digital transformation budget up 12% next year
[Article]
Section: Economy
By: Han Soyun
Published: 2024.11.20 06:40
The government has raised next year's budget for SME digital transformation support by 12% from this year, it was confirmed Wednesday. The program centers on subsidizing part of the cost of adopting e-approval, cloud work tools and payment systems.
The draft budget also adds a new consulting program for companies with fewer than 50 employees, in which specialists accompany applicants from the stage of choosing tools.
"We welcome the increase, but for small companies the application paperwork itself is a burden," said Jeong Hyeonu, head of policy at the Korea SME Federation. "Simplifying the process would make the effect felt."
The head of a manufacturer that took part last year said, "After we got rid of paper approvals, the time spent waiting for sign-off was cut in half."
The budget will be finalized next month after review by the National Assembly.

Teheran-ro office vacancy falls for third straight quarter
[Article]
Section: Real Estate
By: Ryu Dohyeon
Published: 2024.11.19 08:20
Vacancy in large office buildings along Teheran-ro in Seoul's Gangnam district has fallen for a third straight quarter. A third-quarter report released Tuesday by real estate adviser Korea Workspace Institute put vacancy in the area at 4.1%, down 0.5 percentage points from the previous quarter.
Expansion demand from IT and fintech companies drove the decline. New buildings between Yeoksam and Seolleung stations continue to draw inquiries, and some floors were leased before construction began.
"As the share of remote work has stabilized, companies are rearranging space around collaboration rather than cutting it," said Ma Jeonghun, senior researcher at the institute.
Rents also edged up. Monthly rent per 3.3 square meters rose 1.8% from the previous quarter, and effective costs including maintenance fees rose more, the report said.
The institute expects vacancy to hold at the current level or fall slightly in the first half of next year because new supply is limited.

6 in 10 office workers want fewer year-end dinners
[Article]
Section: Society
By: Seo Minji
Published: 2024.11.20 07:00
Six in 10 office workers said they would like fewer year-end company dinners this year than last. The finding comes from a survey of 1,000 workers conducted over five days from the 11th by the Workplace Life Institute.
Some 61% of respondents wanted fewer dinners, citing "lack of personal time after work" (42%) and "cost" (27%). Meanwhile 33% said the current level was about right.
Lunch was the most popular alternative format. More respondents also said they would prefer shared activities such as watching a performance or taking part in a hands-on program.
"Preferences differ by generation, but willingness to take part was high at every age when attendance was not compulsory," said Roh Eunji, a researcher at the institute.
Some companies are moving year-end gatherings into working hours. A mid-sized IT company plans to replace its year-end party with a lunch event this year.

Golf courses compete with winter green-fee discounts
[Article]
Section: Life
By: Ryu Dohyeon
Published: 2024.11.21 07:30
Ahead of the winter off-season, golf courses around the capital region are cutting green fees. According to online booking services, more than 20 courses in the region have announced winter rates this month.
Many are lowering weekday daytime green fees by around 20% from last season, and some add further discounts for two-player rounds or afternoon bookings. A few advertise heater rentals or hot food.
"In winter the number of players falls to about 60% of the summer level," said an official at a golf booking service. "Competition to hold on to demand through price gets earlier every year."
Players have more choices, but rounds are sometimes cancelled during cold snaps, so it is advisable to check cancellation policies in advance.
The industry expects discounts to narrow somewhat after mid-December if year-end group bookings partly recover.

Elementary winter English camps fill up early
[Article]
Section: Education
By: Oh Taegyeong
Published: 2024.11.21 08:00
Winter vacation English camps for elementary school students are filling up within days of opening registration. According to the education industry, many major camps in Seoul and Gyeonggi Province reached capacity this week.
This year, day camps drew more competition than residential ones. Parents are less willing to send children far from home and want to keep daily rhythms during the break.
"Camps that promote native-speaker teachers and small classes have a waiting list on the day registration opens," said an official at an education counseling firm.
Tuition averages around KRW 900,000 for a two-week course, about 5% more than last year. Some parents say they are weighing cost against results.
Experts advise checking instructor qualifications, safety management and refund rules before signing up.

15 million dog owners: pet cafes and treat subscriptions grow
[Article]
Section: Life
By: Han Soyun
Published: 2024.11.18 09:10
As the number of people raising companion animals reaches 15 million, the market for dog-related services is growing fast. An analysis found that pet cafes and treat subscription services are leading the growth.
Pet cafes in major commercial districts of Seoul have grown by nearly 40% over the past two years. Venues that allow dogs inside have become a popular spot for weekend family outings.
Subscriptions that deliver treats and food monthly have also gained members. "Most subscribers stay on for more than a year once they sign up," said an executive at one provider.
"As the market grows, it is time to refine basic rules such as hygiene standards and ingredient labeling," said Do Gyeongah, a director at the Korea Pet Industry Association.
New pet insurance and health checkup products are also appearing, and the market is expected to keep expanding for the time being.

By: Im Junseo

We used CorpX Works 4.0, released in June, for team work for a month. The most noticeable changes are read receipts and the typing indicator in the messenger. You can tell right away whether the other person has read your message, and a marker appears beside the bubble while they are writing a reply.
It felt a little awkward at first. Some on the team said that being read without getting a reply feels like pressure. After about a week, though, unnecessary check-in messages like "I assume they saw it and will handle it" dropped noticeably.
The approval flow got lighter too. With mobile approval, you can receive approval alerts while out of the office and handle them on the spot. When alerts arrive in bunches it is easy to miss an important one, so we had to adjust the notification grouping settings.
On speed, 4.0 is clearly better. Opening a chat window and sending a message after attaching a file both took less time than in the previous version. Search covers message text and attachment names together, but results for older conversations come slowly.
Overall, read receipts divide opinion but speed up communication at work. Larger teams should settle their notification and read-receipt policies before rolling it out.

Impersonation phishing on office messengers rises: "Doubt anyone who asks for a password"
[Article]
Section: Security
By: Jo Haneul
Published: 2024.11.19 09:30
Phishing attempts that impersonate executives or staff from other departments to extract information through office messengers and email are on the rise. Security firms warn they get more frequent at year-end, when workloads peak.
A trend report recently released by the Korea Information Protection Council says reported impersonation phishing cases in the third quarter were up about 30% from a year earlier. Many messages applied time pressure, with lines such as "an urgent approval is needed" or "your account needs to be verified."
"A legitimate security officer will not ask for a password over a messenger," said Seo Jinho, principal researcher at the council. "Whoever asks, you need a habit of calling them directly or checking again through an official internal channel."
Companies are expanding employee training. Some send mock phishing emails and feed the results into education, while others share cases on internal bulletin boards.
Experts advise doubting a sender first even if the profile photo and name look familiar. Reporting a suspicious message to the security team is the fastest response.

Published: 2024.11.20 10:20
The software-as-a-service (SaaS) industry is trimming hiring ahead of year-end. Job platform data show postings by SaaS firms for developers and planners this month were down nearly 15% from the same month last year.
Several companies are putting off new hires until next year's budgets are set. An HR manager at a SaaS firm said, "Funding has turned cautious, so we are keeping headcount plans conservative."
Security is the exception. Postings for security engineers and information protection staff actually rose, as customers increasingly ask during adoption whether a vendor holds security certifications.
The moderators of the job-seeker community Developer Circle said, "The mood among experienced hires is to wait until early next year, and competition for entry-level postings has risen."
The industry expects hiring to revive once budgets are fixed in the first half of next year, but the imbalance in the supply of security staff is likely to persist for now.

Developer survey: "Thursday deploys are the scariest"
[Article]
Section: Development
By: Jo Haneul
Published: 2024.11.20 14:00
Four in 10 developers named Thursday as the most stressful day to deploy, according to a survey of 1,200 members by the developer community Developer Circle.
The top reason for Thursday rather than Friday was that "there is only one day left to clean up before the weekend if something goes wrong." Since many teams ban Friday deploys outright, Thursday effectively becomes the last deployment day, the report explained.
Tuesday was the most comfortable day. Deploying early in the week means the whole team is at work if problems arise, with room to fix and redeploy.
"Since we introduced automatic rollback and staged releases, we don't care much about the day," said a platform team lead at a mid-sized software company. "What matters is how quickly you can revert, not the weekday."
About half of respondents said they do not leave the monitoring screen for 30 minutes after a deploy.

Published: 2024.11.21 09:40
Enterprise work apps are racing to strengthen mobile approval. Receiving an e-approval alert and approving or rejecting it right from a phone has become a baseline feature of corporate collaboration tools.
CorpX Works 4.0, released in June, also added mobile approval. Other vendors are rolling out features such as face-recognition authentication, alert summaries and at-a-glance approval chains.
"With field work and remote work now routine, there is strong demand to keep approvals from becoming a bottleneck," said Choi Daeun, researcher at market research firm Digital Work Research. "The share of mobile approvals has risen noticeably this year."
Security is an issue as well. Lost phones and public Wi-Fi create a risk of data leaks, so companies are increasingly requiring device registration and additional authentication.
The industry expects mobile approval to extend beyond simple sign-off to light edits and comments.
